issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a Stock class (with methods like add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock) as the shared stock type for SealSaloon, but the template repository provides an Inventory class implementing those methods and leaves Stock.java empty. The solution implementation (SealSaloon) also uses Inventory as the stock type. This naming mismatch (Stock vs Inventory) is likely unintentional and will confuse students about which class to use/modify and whether they should implement Stock or Inventory.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming consistent across artifacts. Either: (a) rename Inventory to Stock in the template and solution (adjust filenames and references) so it matches the problem statement/UML, or (b) update the problem statement and UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock and remove or populate the empty Stock.java file. Ensure the class that provides add/take/findStockIngredient/addToStockIngredients/emptyStock is the same named type in the template, solution, and problem description.
